answer: Three established peers check the serial in the public toll registry, the account record, and a fresh signature before a single identity is stamped real. One agent opens one electronic toll account and ties the transponder to that identity, so a copper flood of fakes has to pass a zenith of paperwork: transponder $20 to $40 plus the vehicle itself, and a thousand fakes burns $20,000 to $40,000 and a thousand vehicles, each one waiting on a separate registration. Like a sonnet with a fixed rhyme, one transponder locks one agent to one account no one else can copy.
